title: The Gallery
idiom: ink-and-watercolour root-atlas soil section, a life's works buried in the roots under the house
hero_prompt: Ink and watercolour in the manner of a hand-drawn botanical root atlas, a soil cross-section, hand-made on paper, flat and graphic with visible pen line and watercolour wash, not a photograph, not a 3D render, no depth-of-field, wide panoramic composition: along the top a thin strip of ground with a long low house of many lit windows standing on it; below the ground line, filling most of the frame, a great root system drawn in brown ink spreads from left to right like a long path; caught among the roots, as if the roots had grown from them, lie small buried things in a loose row from left to right: a child's wooden recorder, a plain unmarked black record, a plain cassette, an acoustic guitar, a stack of loose paper tied with string, a small wooden box with two knobs. Warm earth browns, ochre and soft green.
icon_prompt: Linocut emblem, a flat single-colour black silhouette on an ochre ground, no shading or gradients: a thick plain square picture frame, completely empty inside, with one bold root growing down through its opening and out below the frame, branching at its tip. Nothing else: no person, no figure, no animal. Bold, high-contrast, no fine linework, reads clearly at 24 pixels.
